notes:
ACCESS: robots.txt at urbanoutfitters.com/robots.txt is generic 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' (no ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai disallow), so all tiers were permitted. Tier (a) direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi, chrome120 impersonation) got a 403 DataDome CAPTCHA (captcha-delivery.com challenge) on the very first request -> escalated to tier (b). Headless Playwright also hit the DataDome CAPTCHA iframe -> escalated within tier (b) to headed Playwright (headless=False) with --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled plus a navigator.webdriver override, which reached the real site (200, full rendered HTML) consistently for every page fetched; tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome was not needed. TREE METHOD: union of the site's own JSON-LD SiteNavigationElement block (id='#left-navigation', present on /home and every category landing page) which gives the exact 'Home + Dorm' mega-menu tree, plus each relevant category landing page's own left-nav sub-list (same JSON-LD pattern re-appears scoped to that section). Top-level sections checked: Bedding, Furniture, Home Decor (apartment-room-decor), Kitchen + Dining (dinnerware), Wall Art (mirrors-wall-art), Rugs, Bath (bathroom-decor), Storage + Organization; Lighting/Water Bottles+Tumblers/Stationery+Desk Supplies/Electronics+Accessories were skipped as out-of-scope categories. QTY METHOD: rendered '

...

N products

' header text on each individual subcategory listing page (not the parent's aggregate count), taken verbatim; parent/group pages (Bedding=291, Home Decor=288, Kitchen+Dining=155, Wall Art=83, Bath=116, Storage+Organization=81) were used only to build the tree, never recorded as rows since valid subcategories exist under each (parent-URL rule). PRODUCT-LEVEL VERIFICATION: for every ambiguous or mixed-sounding node, sampled actual product alt-text/titles (scrolling to load more of the grid) before deciding, per the ambiguity-handling rule (title/purpose over category label alone). DUPLICATES: /pillows-throw-blankets (Bedding nav 'Pillows + Throws') and /decorative-pillows-throw-blankets (Home Decor nav 'Pillows + Throws') canonicalize to the identical URL/count (84) -> recorded once under Bedding. /kitchen-storage and /kitchen-storage-accessories (Storage+Org nav 'Kitchen Storage' vs Kitchen+Dining nav 'Organization + Accessories') canonicalize to the same URL (21) -> both excluded anyway (see below), so no duplicate emitted. /storage-furniture (Storage+Org nav) and /storage (Furniture nav, same label 'Storage Furniture') canonicalize to the identical URL/count (85) -> single decision made, excluded (see below). EXCLUDED (neither Textile nor Storage): Furniture top-level and all its subcats (Seating, Accent Tables, Desks+Vanities, Dressers, Beds+Headboards) -> Furniture.xlsx territory, not re-checked. Lighting, Water Bottles+Tumblers, Stationery+Desk Supplies, Electronics+Accessories -> own/general-merchandise categories. Home Decor's Decorative Accents, Frames+Photo Displays, Candles+Home Fragrance, Planters+Vases, Plants -> Decorative Home Accessories territory. Home Decor's Hardware -> curtain rods/brackets, explicitly excluded by textile.md 5. Kitchen+Dining's Drinkware, Dinnerware, Serveware, Cookware+Tools, Health+Wellness Snacks -> Kitchen & Dining territory, not storage/textile. Wall Art's Posters+Art, Mirrors, Wallpaper -> Wall Decor, not textile. Wall Art's Tapestries + Wall Accents (/tapestries, h1 'Tapestries & Hanging Wall Decor', 40 products) -> sampled 35+ unique product titles: overwhelmingly non-textile (wall clocks, sports-team metal/tin street signs, wood signs, ceramic wall hangings/tiles) with only ~7-8 genuine fabric items (macrame/tufted/crochet/jute wall hangings, printed tapestries) scattered in; no facet exists to isolate a reliable textile-only count, so per textile.md 14 ('do not classify all Wall Decor as Textile') and the core PRIMARY-PRODUCT-TYPE-over-category-label principle, the whole node was excluded rather than forced in or given a fabricated partial count -> Wall Decor/Decorative Home Accessories territory, already validated elsewhere. STORAGE EXCLUSIONS: 'Storage Furniture' (/storage, 85 products, h1 'Storage Furniture') -> sampled titles are genuine furniture pieces (Jane Upholstered Vanity & Stool Set, Alana Storage Console) and the identical URL is explicitly cross-listed in the site's own Furniture left-nav under the same label -> Furniture.xlsx territory per storage.md 21/27, consistent with how sister-brand Anthropologie (SR7) handled its own 'Storage Furniture, Cabinets & Consoles' Furniture-nav node. 'Wall Storage + Shelving' (/shelving, 40 products, h1 'Wall Storage: Shelves, Hooks & More') -> sampled 34 unique titles: ~82% are decorative wall hooks and figurine/floating-ledge wall shelves (Mid-Century Wall Hook, Florence Figurine Wall Shelf, Fish Metal Wall Hook, Rattan Daisy Wall Shelf, etc.), only a handful of genuine hanging storage caddies/wall cabinet mixed in -> per storage.md 18/19/24 ('do not classify every shelf/rack as Storage merely because it can hold objects'; primarily-decorative wall racks/shelves belong to Wall Decor/Decorative Home Accessories) the whole node was excluded. 'Kitchen Storage & Organization' (/kitchen-storage-accessories, also reached via /kitchen-storage, 21 products, h1 'Kitchen Storage & Organization') -> sampled titles are almost entirely BAGGU/AllSaints reusable tote bags (explicitly excluded as personal-carrying fashion bags per storage.md 6/26), coasters, water-bottle slings, and two 'Kitchen Island' furniture pieces; zero genuine storage bins/containers/organizers found in two full scroll passes -> excluded despite the category's own label, per the PRIMARY-PRODUCT-TYPE-over-category-label principle. 'Jewelry Organizers' (/jewelry-organizers, 41 products) was NOT excluded despite a similar mixed sample (roughly half decorative catch-all/trinket dishes, half genuine lidded jewelry boxes/stands/wall frames) because the ratio was much closer to even (not 'overwhelming' like the two excluded nodes above) and the site's own category name matches storage.md 7's explicit 'Jewelry/Jewellery Organizers' inclusion -> kept at MEDIUM confidence with the mix flagged.
